info.title: IoT Vision Hub
info.summary: Asynchronous camera monitoring: motion events, alerts and live streams.

get.description:
The process is up and serving requests. Never checks dependencies, so a database outage
does not make an orchestrator restart a healthy process.
All dependencies are reachable, so the hub can take traffic. Returns 503 otherwise.

post.description: OAuth2 password flow (form-encoded `username` and `password`). Rate-limited per client.
Exchange a refresh token for a new token pair. The old refresh token stops working.
Revoke the refresh token. The current access token expires on its own within minutes.
Browsers cannot send an `Authorization` header when opening a WebSocket or an `` MJPEG stream; they pass this short-lived, single-use ticket as `?ticket=` instead.
Starts the camera right away when `enabled`.

Open the source and read one frame, without saving anything. A failure is reported in
the body (`ok: false`), not as an HTTP error.

patch.description:
Only fields present in the body change. Changing the source, detection or frame rate
restarts a running camera.

post.description: Accepted: the camera connects in the background; watch `status` become `online`.

put.description:
Hot reload: a running camera restarts with the new settings (its background model
re-learns for a moment).

get.description: At most about a second old (live frames refresh continuously while someone watches).

200.description: JPEG of the latest live frame

get.description:
Newest first. Snapshot links in the response are signed and expire after
`VISION_HUB_SECURITY__SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS`.

Newest first: who changed which device or user, and when. `request_id` matches the
server logs of the request that made the change.
Use directly as ``. Ends when the camera stops.

Use the signed `url` from an event, or a bearer token. Snapshots never change, so
browsers may cache them privately.
